preamble: Rounding of the close back unrounded vowel [ɯ] to [u], merging it with /u/. Proto-Tai had a phonemic *ɯ, which most Tai languages keep as /ɯ/ (Thai ลืม /lɯːm˧/ 'to forget', คืน /kʰɯːn˧/ 'night'). Pittayaporn (2009) shows that its quality was affected by the following consonant. Before the velar stop *-k, long *ɯː became /uː/ in Thai (Siamese) and /u/ in Lungchow. Before *-m, short and long *ɯ became /u/ in many Central and Northern Tai varieties, including Lungchow, Yay and Wuming, the dialect Standard Zhuang is based on. He attributes the rounding before *-m to the labial coda.

examples.note: Before other codas Thai keeps the unrounded vowel: ลืม /lɯːm˧/ 'to forget' (< *lɯːmᴬ), คืน /kʰɯːn˧/ 'night' (< *ɣɯːnᴬ). Lao ຖືກ keeps it in this word.
Lungchow (Longzhou) keeps /ɯː/ in open syllables (*sɯːᴬ 'writing, book' > ɬɯː, tone A1) and lowers it to /ɤ/ before *-n and *-l.
Before other codas Zhuang keeps /ɯ/: hwnz /hɯn˧˩/ 'night' (< *ɣɯːnᴬ), lwg /lɯk˧/ 'child' (< *lɯːkᴰ).

sources: Pittayaporn, P. (2009). The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University. https://hdl.handle.net/1813/13855
